Label: type
Description: Instance-of link. Concepts, property declarations and restrictions are typed owl:Class, owl:ObjectProperty, owl:Restriction and so on; the qualitative value individuals are typed with their *-Constant or UoM-* class.

Label: subclass of
Description: Links a concept to its necessary conditions. About 24,700 triples point straight at a named parent, but most biology concepts point to an anonymous owl:Class whose owl:intersectionOf list holds the named parent(s) and nested owl:Restriction blocks. Reach named parents with rdfs:subClassOf/(owl:intersectionOf/rdf:rest*/rdf:first)* and FILTER(isIRI(?parent)). 197 axioms run the other way, from an anonymous class to a named concept: these are sufficient conditions ('triggers'), meaning anything matching the description is an instance of that concept.

Label: intersection of
Description: Links an anonymous owl:Class to an RDF list (rdf:first/rdf:rest) of the classes and restrictions it conjoins. This is how each concept bundles its named parents with its relation axioms; the lists nest several levels deep.

Label: union of
Description: Links an anonymous owl:Class to an RDF list of alternative classes. Rare: 14 uses.

Label: first
Description: The member at the head of an RDF list, used to walk owl:intersectionOf and owl:unionOf lists.

Label: rest
Description: The remainder of an RDF list (rdf:nil at the end). Use rdf:rest*/rdf:first to enumerate every member.

Label: on property
Description: The aura relation an owl:Restriction constrains, e.g. aura:has-part. This is the only place the roughly 280 aura relations appear: none of them is asserted as a direct subject-predicate-object triple.

Label: some values from
Description: The filler of an existential restriction: every instance of the restricted concept has at least one value of the restricted relation drawn from this class. Usually an anonymous owl:Class wrapping a named class (and an aura:ID-N prototype marker), so follow it with (owl:intersectionOf/rdf:rest*/rdf:first)* and FILTER(isIRI(?filler)).

Label: has value
Description: The fixed value of a value restriction: a named individual (e.g. a *-Constant) or a literal such as a number or name string.

Label: on class
Description: The class a qualified cardinality restriction counts.

Label: qualified cardinality
Description: Exact number of values of the restricted relation that belong to the owl:onClass class.

Label: min qualified cardinality
Description: Minimum number of values of the restricted relation that belong to the owl:onClass class.

Label: max qualified cardinality
Description: Maximum number of values of the restricted relation that belong to the owl:onClass class.

Label: disjoint with
Description: States that two named concepts share no instances, e.g. Mitochondrion is disjoint with Nucleus, Plastid and Vesicle.

Label: domain
Description: Declared domain class of an aura relation.

Label: range
Description: Declared range class of an aura relation.

Label: subproperty of
Description: Declares an aura relation a specialisation of another, e.g. first-subevent is a subproperty of subevent.

Label: inverse of
Description: Declares two aura relations inverses of each other (asserted for two pairs only; most inverses follow the X / X-of naming convention instead).

Label: comment
Description: Used once, on the ontology header, for the Vulcan Inc. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 licence notice. Concept definitions are in aura:description and aura:user-description instead.

Description: Short textbook-style definition of a concept, written by the KB's biologist encoders. Present on about 5,700 concepts; the best source of a human-readable definition.

Label: description
Description: Longer definition of a concept or relation, often quoting the source text (e.g. Alberts, Essential Cell Biology). Present on about 160 concepts; some values have their spaces stripped.

Label: in concept
Description: Links an aura:ID-N node-marker class to the concept in which that node was introduced (about 21,000 markers).

Label: prototype node
Description: The original AURA prototype-node identifier (a string such as "_Energy-Transformation-by-Organism33214") of an aura:ID-N marker class.

Label: OWL class
Description: Every biology concept (about 6,300 named, plus about 21,000 aura:ID-N prototype-node markers and many anonymous class expressions) is an owl:Class. KB Bio 101 is an ontology: concepts are classes, not instances.

Label: OWL restriction
Description: Anonymous class expression (about 81,600) that carries a concept's relation axioms: owl:onProperty names the aura relation and owl:someValuesFrom, owl:hasValue or owl:onClass plus a cardinality gives the filler.

Label: object property
Description: Declared aura relation between concepts (353).

Label: datatype property

Label: annotation property
Description: Declared aura annotation property (5: concept2words, description, in-concept, prototype-node, user-description).

Label: functional property
Description: aura relation that takes at most one value (127).

Label: transitive property
Description: Transitive aura relation (17).

Label: Aggregate groundwater use (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type AG: An Aggregate Groundwater Withdrawal/Return site represents an aggregate of specific sites whe groundwater is withdrawn or returned which is defined by a geographic area or some other common characteristic. An aggregate groundwatergroundwater site type is used when it is not possible or practical to describe the specific sites as springs or as any type of well including 'multiple wells', or when water-use information is only available for the aggregate. Aggregate sites that span multiple counties should be coded with 000 as the county code, or an aggregate site can be created for each county.

Label: Aggregate surface-water-use (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type AS: An Aggregate Surface-Water Diversion/Return site represents an aggregate of specific sites where surface water is diverted or returned which is defined by a geographic area or some other common characteristic. An aggregate surface-water site type is used when it is not possible or practical to describe the specific sites as diversions, outfalls, or land application sites, or when water-use information is only available for the aggregate. Aggregate sites that span multiple counties should be coded with 000 as the county code, or an aggregate site can be created for each county.

Label: Atmosphere (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type AT: A site established primarily to measure meteorological properties or atmospheric deposition.

Label: Estuary (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type ES: A coastal inlet of the sea or ocean; esp. the mouth of a river, where tide water normally mixes with stream water (modified, Webster). Salinity in estuaries typically ranges from 1 to 25 Practical Salinity Units (psu), as compared oceanic values around 35-psu. See also: tidal stream and coastal.

Label: Animal waste lagoon (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-AWL: A facility for storage and/or biological treatment of wastes from livestock operations. Animal-waste lagoons are earthen structures ranging from pits to large ponds, and contain manure which has been diluted with building washwater, rainfall, and surface runoff. In treatment lagoons, the waste becomes partially liquefied and stabilized by bacterial action before the waste is disposed of on the land and the water is discharged or re-used.

Label: Cistern (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-CI: An artificial, non-pressurized reservoir filled by gravity flow and used for water storage. The reservoir may be located above, at, or below ground level. The water may be supplied from diversion of precipitation, surface, or groundwater sources.

Label: Combined sewer (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-CS: An underground conduit created to convey storm drainage and waste products into a wastewater-treatment plant, stream, reservoir, or disposal site.

Label: Diversion (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-DV: A site where water is withdrawn or diverted from a surface-water body (e.g. the point where the upstream end of a canal intersects a stream, or point where water is withdrawn from a reservoir). Includes sites where water is pumped for use elsewhere, and sites where the surface-water body is considered a groundwater source such as a mining excavation with no surface-water inflow.

Label: Field, Pasture, Orchard, or Nursery (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-FON: A water-using agricultural facility characterized by an area for crop cultivation (field), grazing (pasture), fruit or nut production (orchard), or plant propagation (nursery). Irrigation water may or may not be applied.

Label: Golf course (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-GC: A place-of-use, either public or private, where the game of golf is played. A golf course typically uses water for irrigation purposes. Should not be used if the site is a specific hydrologic feature or facility; but can be used especially for the water-use sites.

Label: Landfill (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-LF: A typically dry location on the surface of the land where primarily solid waste products are currently, or previously have been, aggregated and sometimes covered with a veneer of soil. See also: Wastewater disposal and waste-injection well.

Label: Outfall (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-OF: A site where water or wastewater is returned to a surface-water body, e.g. the point where wastewater is returned to a stream. Typically, the discharge end of an effluent pipe.

Label: Pavement (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-PV: A surface site where the land surface is covered by a relatively impermeable material, such as concrete or asphalt. Pavement sites are typically part of transportation infrastructure, such as roadways, parking lots, or runways.

Label: Laboratory or sample-preparation area (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-QC: A site where some types of quality-control samples are collected, and where equipment and supplies for environmental sampling are prepared. Equipment blank samples are commonly collected at this site type, as are samples of locally produced deionized water. This site type is typically used when the data are either not associated with a unique environmental data-collection site, or where blank water supplies are designated by Center offices with unique station IDs.

Label: Wastewater sewer (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-SEW: An underground conduit created to convey liquid and semisolid domestic, commercial, or industrial waste into a treatment plant, stream, reservoir, or disposal site. If the sewer also conveys storm water, then the "combined sewer" secondary site type should be used.

Label: Septic system (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-SPS: A site within or in close proximity to a subsurface sewage disposal system that generally consists of: (1) a septic tank where settling of solid material occurs, (2) a distribution system that transfers fluid from the tank to (3) a leaching system that disperses the effluent into the ground.

Label: Storm sewer (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-STS: An underground conduit created to convey storm drainage into a stream channel or reservoir. If the sewer also conveys liquid waste products, then the "combined sewer" secondary site type should be used.

Label: Water-distribution system (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-WDS: A site located somewhere on a networked infrastructure that distributes treated or untreated water to multiple domestic, industrial, institutional, and (or) commercial users. May be owned by a municipality or community, a water district, or a private concern.

Label: Waste injection well (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-WIW: A facility used to convey industrial waste, domestic sewage, brine, mine drainage, radioactive waste, or other fluid into an underground zone. An oil-test or deep-water well converted to waste disposal should be in this category. A well where fresh water is injected to artificially recharge thegroundwaterr supply or to pressurize an oil or gas production zone by injecting a fluid should be classified as a well (not an injection-well facility), with additional information recorded under Use of Site.

Label: Water-use establishment (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-WU: A place-of-use (a water using facility that is associated with a specific geographical point location, such as a business or industrial user) that cannot be specified with any other facility secondary type. Water-use place-of-use sites are establishments such as a factory, mill, store, warehouse, farm, ranch, or bank. A place-of-use site is further classified using the national water-use category code (C39) and optionally classified using the Standard Industrial Classification System Code (SIC code) or North American Classification System Code (NAICS code). See also: Aggregate water-use-establishment.

Label: Wastewater land application (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type FA-WWD: A site where the disposal of waste water on land occurs. Use "waste-injection well" for underground waste-disposal sites.

Label: Glacier (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GL: Body of land ice that consists of recrystallized snow accumulated on the surface of the ground and moves slowly downslope (WSP-1541A) over a period of years or centuries. Since glacial sites move, the lat-long precision for these sites is usually coarse.

Label: Well (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW: A hole or shaft constructed in the earth intended to be used to locate, sample, or develop groundwater, oil, gas, or some other subsurface material. The diameter of a well is typically much smaller than the depth. Wells are also used to artificially recharge groundwater or to pressurize oil and gas production zones. Additional information about specific kinds of wells should be recorded under the secondary site types or the Use of Site field. Underground waste-disposal wells should be classified as waste-injection wells.

Label: Collector or Ranney type well (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW-CR: An infiltration gallery consisting of one or more underground laterals through which groundwater is collected and a vertical caisson from which groundwater is removed. Also known as a "horizontal well". These wells produce large yield with small drawdown.

Label: Extensometer well (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW-EX: A well equipped to measure small changes in the thickness of the penetrated sediments, such as those caused by groundwater withdrawal or recharge.

Label: Hyporheic-zone well (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW-HZ: A permanent well, drive point, or other device intended to sample a saturated zone in close proximity to a stream.

Label: Interconnected wells (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW-IW: Collector or drainage wells connected by an underground lateral.

Label: Multiple wells (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW-MW: A group of wells that are pumped through a single header and for which little or no data about the individual wells are available.

Label: Test hole not completed as a well (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type GW-TH: An uncased hole (or one cased only temporarily) that was drilled for water, or for geologic or hydrogeologic testing. It may be equipped temporarily with a pump in order to make a pumping test, but if the hole is destroyed after testing is completed, it is still a test hole. A core hole drilled as a part of mining or quarrying exploration work should be in this class.

Label: Land (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA: A location on the surface of the earth that is not normally saturated with water. Land sites are appropriate for sampling vegetation, overland flow of water, or measuring land-surface properties such as temperature. (See also: Wetland).

Label: Excavation (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-EX: An artificially constructed cavity in the earth that is deeper than the soil (see soil hole), larger than a well bore (see well and test hole), and substantially open to the atmosphere. The diameter of an excavation is typically similar or larger than the depth. Excavations include building-foundation diggings, roadway cuts, and surface mines.

Label: Outcrop (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-OU: The part of a rock formation that appears at the surface of the surrounding land.

Label: Playa (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-PLY: A dried-up, vegetation-free, flat-floored area composed of thin, evenly stratified sheets of fine clay, silt or sand, and represents the bottom part of a shallow, completely closed or undrained desert lake basin in which water accumulates and is quickly evaporated, usually leaving deposits of soluble salts.

Label: Soil hole (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-SH: A small excavation into soil at the top few meters of earth surface. Soil generally includes some organic matter derived from plants. Soil holes are created to measure soil composition and properties. Sometimes electronic probes are inserted into soil holes to measure physical properties, and (or) the extracted soil is analyzed.

Label: Sinkhole (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-SNK: A crater formed when the roof of a cavern collapses; usually found in limestone areas. Surface water and precipitation that enters a sinkhole usually evaporates or infiltrates into the ground, rather than draining into a stream.

Label: Shore (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-SR: The land along the edge of the sea, a lake, or a wide river where the investigator considers the proximity of the water body to be important. Land adjacent to a reservoir, lake, impoundment, or oceanic site type is considered part of the shore when it includes a beach or bank between the high and low water marks.

Label: Volcanic vent (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LA-VOL: Vent from which volcanic gases escape to the atmosphere. Also known as fumarole.

Label: Lake, Reservoir, Impoundment (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type LK: An inland body of standing fresh or saline water that is generally too deep to permit submerged aquatic vegetation to take root across the entire body (cf: wetland). This site type includes an expanded part of a river, a reservoir behind a dam, and a natural or excavated depression containing a water body without surface-water inlet and/or outlet.

Label: Ocean (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type OC: Site in the open ocean, gulf, or sea. (See also: Coastal, Estuary, and Tidal stream).

Label: Coastal (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type OC-CO: An oceanic site that is located off-shore beyond the tidal mixing zone (estuary) but close enough to the shore that the investigator considers the presence of the coast to be important. Coastal sites typically are within three nautical miles of the shore.

Label: Subsurface (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type SB: A location below the land surface, but not a well, soil hole, or excavation.

Label: Cave (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type SB-CV: A natural open space within a rock formation large enough to accommodate a human. A cave may have an opening to the outside, is always underground, and sometimes submerged. Caves commonly occur by the dissolution of soluble rocks, generally limestone, but may also be created within the voids of large-rock aggregations, in openings along seismic faults, and in lava formations.

Label: Groundwater drain (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type SB-GWD: An underground pipe or tunnel through which groundwater is artificially diverted to surface water for the purpose of reducing erosion or lowering the water table. A drain is typically open to the atmosphere at the lowest elevation, in contrast to a well which is open at the highest point.

Label: Tunnel, shaft, or mine (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type SB-TSM: A constructed subsurface open space large enough to accommodate a human that is not substantially open to the atmosphere and is not a well. The excavation may have been for minerals, transportation, or other purposes. See also: Excavation.

Label: Unsaturated zone (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type SB-UZ: A site equipped to measure conditions in the subsurface deeper than a soil hole, but above the water table or other zone of saturation.

Label: Spring (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type SP: A location at which the water table intersects the land surface, resulting in a natural flow of groundwater to the surface. Springs may be perennial, intermittent, or ephemeral.

Label: Stream (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type ST: A body of running water moving under gravity flow in a defined channel. The channel may be entirely natural, or altered by engineering practices through straightening, dredging, and (or) lining. An entirely artificial channel should be qualified with the "canal" or "ditch" secondary site type.

Label: Canal (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type ST-CA: An artificial watercourse designed for navigation, drainage, or irrigation by connecting two or more bodies of water; it is larger than a ditch.

Label: Ditch (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type ST-DCH: An excavation artificially dug in the ground, either lined or unlined, for conveying water for drainage or irrigation; it is smaller than a canal.

Label: Tidal stream (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type ST-TS: A stream reach where the flow is influenced by the tide, but where the water chemistry is not normally influenced. A site where ocean water typically mixes with stream water should be coded as an estuary.

Label: Wetland (USGS site type)
Description: USGS site type WE: Land where saturation with water is the dominant factor determining the nature of soil development and the types of plant and animal communities living in the soil and on its surface (Cowardin, December 1979). Wetlands are found from the tundra to the tropics and on every continent except Antarctica. Wetlands are areas that are inundated or saturated by surface or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and that under normal circumstances do support, a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions. Wetlands generally include swamps, marshes, bogs and similar areas. Wetlands may be forested or unforested, and naturally or artificially created.

Label: Hydrometric Feature (Application Schema)

Label: hyf:HY_FlowPath
Description: The HY_Flowpath feature type realizes a catchment specifically as a path connecting the inflow and outflow of the catchment it realizes. HY_Flowpath specializes HY_CatchmentRealization with respect to an implied linear geometric representation including a straight or curved line. Topologically, the flowpath connects the inflow and outflow of the catchment, and is understood as an edge bounded by an inflow node and an outflow node, and corresponding to left-bank and right-bank catchment faces. Hydrologically, the flowpath is a line describing a moving particle of water.  Through generalization, HY_Flowpath inherits the shape and the realizedCatchment properties. The optional shape of the flowpath is usually a single curve.

Label: ReferenceLocation
Description: The HY_HydroLocation feature type (Figure 35) conceptualizes the idea that a hydro nexus can be realized by practically any feature of interest. The hydro nexus concept is used to define the hydrologic determination of a catchment but, like the catchment concept, does not have inherent realization(s). Any hydrologically significant feature that can be identified as (said to be) the outlet of a catchment may realize the hydro nexus. Typically, this will be a permanent, stable location that is fixed and/or referenced by coordinates.  Landmarks such as confluences, points corresponding to vertical sections, or the position of a monitoring station on a river are typical realizations of the hydro nexus. Other kinds of hydro nexus realizations that don't carry normal surface water characteristics as defined in this standard, e.g. a spring where groundwater enters the surface, an arbitrary point projected onto the surface, or a nexus that collects many disjoint locations may use or specialize the general HY_HydroLocation type.  Topologically, the HY_HydroLocation should be understood to be the boundary of the corresponding catchment, and always of lower topological dimension than the catchment. Even though the topological realization of a hydro nexus is typically as a node between catchment edges, a nexus realization may also have any geometric representation, including a single point. In many cases, HY_HydroLocations are known but corresponding catchments and hydro nexuses are not defined. For example, stream gages that are part of a catchment dataset whose hydro nexus features are realized by confluences. Both the stream gages and confluences are HY_HydroLocations, but the stream gages’ hydro nexus features are not defined. Using this concept, HY_HydroLocation is expected to be used to link between datasets that have catchments delineated for different HY_HydroLocations. HY_HydroLocation carries two attributes: shape and hydroLocationType. It has referencedPosition and realizedNexus associations implying the hydro-complex feature collection.

Label: hyf:HY_WaterBody

Label: GeoShape (malformed IRI)

Label: indirect position
Description: The HY_IndirectPosition feature type defines the location referenced along an axis, without the necessity of a geometric realization. Indirect position uses a catchment-specific reference system which defines the flowpath as the required linear element along which the position is determined. The indirect position is then expressed as the distance from the upstream and/or downstream end of the flowpath, or from a referent that is already located on that flowpath.  The (indirect) position of an outflow node referenced along an upstream oriented flowpath can be expressed as the distance from an upstream inflow node located on that flowpath, while the (indirect) position of an inflow node referenced along a downstream oriented flowpath can be expressed as distance from a downstream outflow node located on the flowpath. An ‘intermediate’ position referencing known inflow and outflow nodes bounding a flowpath at both ends can be expressed as part of the distance along the entire flowpath, measured from the upstream end of an upstream flowpath, and/or from the downstream end of a downstream flowpath. A position referencing an already referenced location on the flowpath can be expressed as part of the distance along the entire flowpath, measured from the ‘located referent’.   HY_IndirectPosition carries the distanceExpression, and distanceDescription attributes, and has linearElement, locatedReferent and a referenceLocation associations. A point-referent constraint emphasizes the topological relationship between the linear element and point representation of the reference location; a measure-along-flowpath constraint defines the flowpath as the linear element to be used whenever a position is expressed as a distance from a referent.

Label: Glycoprotein
Description: A glycosylation record for a human protein, not the protein itself: one node per reported glycosylation observation (74,722 nodes for 8,112 proteins). IRI http://glygen.org/glycoprotein/<UniProt isoform accession>-<n>. Each record has exactly one evidence (PubMed), at most one glycosylation site, the protein isoform and a Protein Ontology entry. To count glycoproteins, count distinct gly:has_pro_entry values. There is no direct edge to up:Protein: rewrite http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PR_<accession> to http://purl.uniprot.org/uniprot/<accession> to reach the protein, its names and its gene.

Label: Glycosylation Site
Description: An amino acid residue of a protein that carries a glycan. One node per glycosylation record (67,510 nodes covering 22,392 distinct protein positions), IRI http://glygen.org/glycosylationsite/GLYCOSITE_<isoform>-<n>_<position>. The residue number and amino acid are on the faldo:location node; the attached glycan, when reported (62,732 sites), is given by has_saccharide.

Label: Saccharide
Description: A glycan structure, identified by its GlyTouCan accession in the IRI (http://glygen.org/glycan/G49108TO); 1,248 glycans. The rdfs:label gives the monosaccharide composition followed by the glycosylation type and subtype, for example "Hex5HexNAc4 (N-linked, Biantennary)" or "HexNAc1 (O-linked, O-GlcNAc)". The graph holds no structure encoding, mass or other glycan property; filter on the label to select N-linked or O-linked glycans.

Label: Evidence
Description: A publication supporting a glycosylation record or site annotation. The node carries no properties; the PubMed identifier is in the IRI (http://glygen.org/evidence/PubMed_<PMID>). 1,516 publications.

Label: Amino Acid
Description: The amino acid at a modified residue. Ten nodes with no properties, named in the IRI by three-letter code (http://glygen.org/aminoacid/Asn, Ser, Thr, Tyr, Trp, Lys, Cys); a few site annotations use one-letter duplicates (aminoacid/S, T, N), so match both forms.

Label: Protein
Description: A human UniProtKB protein that has glycosylation data in GlyGen (8,112 proteins), IRI http://purl.uniprot.org/uniprot/<accession>. Carries the recommended name as rdfs:label, the UniProt mnemonic, structured names, the encoding gene, the organism and one sequence.

Label: Gene
Description: The gene encoding a protein (8,097 nodes), IRI <protein IRI>#gene-MD5<hash>. The gene symbol is in skos:prefLabel and synonyms in skos:altLabel; hasLocus links to the Ensembl gene and its chromosomal coordinates.

Label: Simple Sequence
Description: An amino acid sequence of a protein isoform (8,111 nodes), IRI http://purl.uniprot.org/isoforms/<accession>-<n>, with the sequence in rdf:value. Each protein links to only one sequence and it is the canonical isoform for just 1,170 proteins (gly:canonical true); for the rest it is an alternative isoform or a related UniProt entry, so check gly:canonical before treating a sequence as the reference for site positions. Many isoform IRIs used by glycosylation records and site regions are not typed with this class.

Label: Structured Name
Description: A resource that holds one name of a protein (recommended or alternative); the text is in up:fullName. IRI <protein IRI>#SIP<hash>.

Label: Taxon
Description: The organism of a protein. The graph contains a single taxon, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon_9606 (Homo sapiens, human).

Label: Gene Locus
Description: The genomic locus of a gene, identified by its Ensembl gene IRI (http://rdf.ebi.ac.uk/resource/ensembl/ENSG00000132703); 7,959 loci. Carries the chromosome, the strand and a gene range with begin and end coordinates. The genome assembly is not stated in the graph.

Label: Region (gene range)
Description: A region describes a length of sequence with a start position and end position; here the chromosomal extent of a gene locus (7,959 nodes, IRI http://purl.uniprot.org/range/<id>). Note the namespace: this is the standard http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (no www); protein-site coordinates use the separate www.biohackathon.org variant.

Label: Exact Position (chromosome)
Description: A position that is exactly known; here the begin or end chromosome coordinate of a gene range (15,896 nodes, IRI http://purl.uniprot.org/position/<id>). Note the namespace: this is the standard http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (no www); protein-site coordinates use the separate www.biohackathon.org variant.

Label: Region (protein site)
Description: A region of a protein isoform sequence annotated with a sequence variant, a phosphorylation site or a glycosylation site annotation (7,874 nodes, IRI http://glygen.org/location/SITE_<isoform>_<begin>_<end>). Nearly all are single residues. This release holds one site region per isoform, so it is a sample of the site data rather than a complete list. Note the namespace: this term uses http://www.biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (with www), which is distinct from the standard FALDO namespace used for gene coordinates.

Label: Exact Position (glycosylation site)
Description: The exact residue position of a glycosylation site on the isoform its record refers to (67,510 nodes, IRI http://glygen.org/location/EXACTPOS_GLYCOSITE_<isoform>-<n>_<position>), with the residue number and the amino acid. Note the namespace: this term uses http://www.biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (with www), which is distinct from the standard FALDO namespace used for gene coordinates.

Label: glycosylated at
Description: Links a glycosylation record to the site on the protein where the glycan is attached. 67,510 of the 74,722 records have a site; the others report glycosylation of the protein without a position.

Label: has saccharide
Description: The glycan attached at a glycosylation site. Present on 62,732 of 67,510 sites; a site without it is a known glycosylation position with no glycan structure reported.

Label: has saccharide
Description: Also used on an untyped glycosylation-site annotation node (IRI http://glygen.org/glycosylationsite/GLYCOSITE_<isoform>_<begin>_<end>) reached from a protein site region (68 triples).

Label: has evidence
Description: The publication supporting a glycosylation record; every record has exactly one. A site reported by several papers appears as several records.

Label: has evidence
Description: Also used on the untyped site annotation nodes reached from a protein site region: phosphorylation sites (260 triples), glycosylation-site annotations (70) and SNVs (12).

Label: has PRO entry
Description: The Protein Ontology entry of the glycosylated protein, an untyped IRI http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PR_<UniProt accession>. This is the only reliable key from a glycosylation record to its protein: replace the PR_ prefix with http://purl.uniprot.org/uniprot/ to get the up:Protein IRI (all 8,112 resolve).

Label: location
Description: Links a glycosylation site to its exact position on the protein sequence. Note the namespace: this term uses http://www.biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (with www), which is distinct from the standard FALDO namespace used for gene coordinates.

Label: position (protein sequence)
Description: The 1-based residue number of a glycosylation site on the isoform its glycosylation record refers to (integer). Note the namespace: this term uses http://www.biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (with www), which is distinct from the standard FALDO namespace used for gene coordinates.

Label: position (protein sequence)
Description: Also the residue number (integer) on the untyped begin and end nodes of a protein site region (IRI http://glygen.org/location/<isoform>_<position>).

Label: has amino acid
Description: The amino acid at a glycosylation site position, for example Asn for N-linked and Ser or Thr for O-linked glycans.

Label: has amino acid
Description: Also the modified amino acid on untyped phosphorylation-site nodes (302 triples) and glycosylation-site annotation nodes (99) reached from a protein site region.

Label: label
Description: The recommended full name of the protein, for example "Serum amyloid P-component".

Label: label
Description: The glycan's composition with its glycosylation type and subtype, for example "Hex5HexNAc4 (N-linked, Biantennary)". Three glycans have no label.

Label: label
Description: The name of the organism ("Homo sapiens").

Label: mnemonic
Description: An easy to remember identifier for a UniProtKB entry, for example SAMP_HUMAN. It is not a stable identifier; use the accession in the protein IRI to identify entries.

Label: recommended name
Description: The name recommended by the UniProt consortium, as a structured name node whose text is in up:fullName.

Label: alternative name
Description: A synonym of the recommended name, as a structured name node whose text is in up:fullName.

Label: full name
Description: The full text of a protein name.

Label: encoded by
Description: The gene by which a protein is encoded.

Label: organism
Description: The organism in which a protein occurs; always human (NCBITaxon_9606) in this graph.

Label: scientific name
Description: The scientific name of the organism ("Homo sapiens").

Label: common name
Description: The common name of the organism ("Human").

Label: sequence
Description: The amino acid sequence node of the protein; one per protein. It is the canonical isoform for only 1,170 proteins (see gly:canonical), and for about 2,000 proteins the isoform IRI carries the accession of a different UniProt entry.

Label: sequence
Description: The protein isoform a glycosylation record refers to, http://purl.uniprot.org/isoforms/<accession>-<n> (isoform 1 for 95% of records). Only 7,417 of the 74,722 records point to an isoform node that is typed and carries a sequence, so do not join records to proteins through this predicate; use gly:has_pro_entry.

Label: value
Description: The amino acid sequence in one-letter code.

Label: canonical
Description: Whether the sequence is the canonical isoform of its UniProt entry (boolean). True for 1,170 of the 8,111 sequences.

Label: preferred label
Description: The gene symbol, for example APCS.

Label: alternative label
Description: A synonym of the gene symbol.

Label: has locus
Description: Links a gene to its genomic locus, an Ensembl gene. Present for 7,959 of 8,097 genes.

Label: chromosome
Description: The chromosome the gene lies on, as a string ("1" to "22", "X", "Y", "MT").

Label: reverse strand
Description: True when the gene is on the reverse strand of the chromosome (boolean).

Label: gene range
Description: The chromosomal region spanned by the gene, with begin and end coordinates.

Label: begin (gene range)
Description: The inclusive beginning of the gene range, as a chromosome position node. Note the namespace: this is the standard http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (no www); protein-site coordinates use the separate www.biohackathon.org variant.

Label: end (gene range)
Description: The inclusive end of the gene range, as a chromosome position node. Note the namespace: this is the standard http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (no www); protein-site coordinates use the separate www.biohackathon.org variant.

Label: position (chromosome)
Description: The chromosome coordinate of a gene range boundary (integer, 1-based). Note the namespace: this is the standard http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo# (no www); protein-site coordinates use the separate www.biohackathon.org variant.

Label: has site
Description: Links a protein isoform to an annotated site region (variant, phosphorylation or glycosylation annotation). Only 1,085 of the 7,874 subjects are typed up:Simple_Sequence; the rest are untyped isoform IRIs with no other triples. To reach the protein, take the accession from the isoform IRI (http://purl.uniprot.org/isoforms/<accession>-<n>) and build http://purl.uniprot.org/uniprot/<accession>.

Label: begin (protein site)
Description: The first residue of a protein site region: an untyped node http://glygen.org/location/<isoform>_<position> whose residue number is in faldo:position. Label: hyf:HY_Catchment
Description: The Catchment model conceptualizes the hydrologic determination of a catchment through inflow and outflow hydro nexus features with the role of getting flow from a contributing catchment, or providing inflow to a receiving catchment (Figure 25 and Figure 26). Conceptually, each catchment has an outflow hydro nexus, and any hydro nexus has a corresponding catchment, even if catchment and/or hydro nexus may not be present in a particular application. A catchment interacts with upper and lower catchments via associated hydro nexuses, and ultimately contributes flow to the hydro nexus of a containing catchment. The catchment should be understood as the logical link between two hydro nexuses. The HY_Catchment feature type captures the union of catchment and hydro nexus, and the multiple realizations of the holistic catchment concept. These realizations include both topological realizations, as well as their geometric representation. HY_Catchment may be further specialized with respect to catchment interaction.  The HY_Catchment feature type (Figure 26) specializes the general HY_HydroFeature type. Through generalization, HY_Catchment inherits the name property. It carries a code attribute and the associations: outflow, inflow, containingCatchment, containedCatchment, conjointCatchment, upperCatchment, lowerCatchment, catchmentRealization. Declared in the schema but not populated in the current release.

Label: hyf:HY_CatchmentRealization
Description: The HY_CatchmentRealization feature type (Figure 34) is based on the idea that there are multiple hydrology-specific perspectives of the holistic catchment concept that are used to describe a catchment as a unit of study shared across sub-domains and studies.  A given catchment realization exists within a hydrologic complex in that, if a catchment realization exists, it exists in the same hydrologic complex as the catchment it realizes. In this way, any realization of a catchment has the same hydrologic determination of the catchment it realizes. If a catchment is connected with other catchments via inflow and/or outflow hydro nexuses, its realizations are also connected. A realization of the logical catchment is always of higher topological dimension than the realization of the corresponding hydro nexus topological boundary. For example, a linear flowpath realizing a catchment may be understood as an edge between inflow and outflow nodes; the areal realization of a catchment as a face bounded by linear inflow and outflow. The catchment realization features defined in this standard refer to objects on the land surface for the purpose of surface water hydrology. In other contexts, other types of catchment realization may exist. Catchment realizations that do not conform to those defined in this standard, for instance realizations in 3- or 4-dimensional perspectives, may be implemented using the general HY_CatchmentRealization type. HY_CatchmentRealization carries a shape attribute and as a realizedCatchment association.

Label: hyf:HY_FlowPath
Description: The HY_Flowpath feature type realizes a catchment specifically as a path connecting the inflow and outflow of the catchment it realizes. HY_Flowpath specializes HY_CatchmentRealization with respect to an implied linear geometric representation including a straight or curved line. Topologically, the flowpath connects the inflow and outflow of the catchment, and is understood as an edge bounded by an inflow node and an outflow node, and corresponding to left-bank and right-bank catchment faces. Hydrologically, the flowpath is a line describing a moving particle of water.  Through generalization, HY_Flowpath inherits the shape and the realizedCatchment properties. The optional shape of the flowpath is usually a single curve.

As a subclass of 'affective process', subjective affective feelings have valence. Valence refers to the 'the subjective value of an event, object, person, or other entity in the life space of the individual' (https://dictionary.apa.org/valence). Valence ranges from negative to positive.

Description: Agency, organization or research group behind the dataset (e.g., USEPA, USGS, iNaturalist) (string)

Label: API URL
Description: URL of the weather archive API request for the site's coordinates (string)

Label: County FIPS
Description: Five-digit county FIPS code (string)

Label: Created At
Description: Time the observation record was created in the knowledge network (dateTime)

Label: Data Type
Description: Kind of data in the dataset: occurrence or density (string)

Label: Dataset Citations
Description: Citation for the dataset; a dataset can have several (string)

Label: Dataset URLs
Description: URL of the dataset or its source; a dataset can have several (string)

Label: Decimal Latitudes
Description: Latitude of the observed organism in decimal degrees, on the reified OBSERVED_ORGANISM link; present on a small share of links (double)

Label: Decimal Longitudes
Description: Longitude of the observed organism in decimal degrees, on the reified OBSERVED_ORGANISM link; present on a small share of links (double)

Label: Download Date
Description: Date the dataset was downloaded from its source (date)

Label: Geometry as WKT
Description: Geometry as Well-Known Text in longitude latitude order: a point for a site, a boundary polygon for a county or state (wktLiteral)

Label: Geometry as WKT
Description: Geometry as Well-Known Text in longitude latitude order: a point for a site, a boundary polygon for a county or state (wktLiteral)

Label: Geometry as WKT
Description: Geometry as Well-Known Text in longitude latitude order: a point for a site, a boundary polygon for a county or state (wktLiteral)

Label: KnowWhereGraph IRI
Description: IRI of the matching KnowWhereGraph administrative region (administrativeRegion.USA.<fips>); the join key to other spatial graphs (IRI)

Label: KnowWhereGraph IRI
Description: IRI of the matching KnowWhereGraph administrative region (administrativeRegion.USA.<fips>); the join key to other spatial graphs (IRI)

Label: Latitude (4 decimals)
Description: Latitude of the site rounded to four decimals, as used in the site key (double)

Label: Latitude
Description: Latitude of the site in decimal degrees (double)

Label: Longitude (4 decimals)
Description: Longitude of the site rounded to four decimals, as used in the site key (double)

Label: Longitude
Description: Longitude of the site in decimal degrees (double)

Label: Measurement Result
Description: Measured value for the observed organism, e.g. a density; the text NA for occurrence records (double)

Label: Measurement Type
Description: Kind of measurement on the link: occurrence or density (string)

Label: Measurement Unit
Description: Unit of the measurement result (individuals/unit_sampling_effort); the text NA for occurrence records (string)

Label: Observation ID
Description: Source identifier of the observation, built from the site, date and dataset; present on a small share of observations (string)

Label: Old Name
Description: County name without the state, e.g. Tippecanoe where the label is Tippecanoe (Indiana) (string)

Label: Program Name
Description: Monitoring programme the dataset comes from (e.g., National Rivers and Streams Assessment, BioData, iNaturalist) (string)

Label: Sampling Effort
Description: Amount of sampling effort behind the measurement; the text NA for occurrence records (double)

Label: Sampling Effort Unit
Description: Unit of the sampling effort (Area Sampled (m^2), Minutes, Number of Hauls); the text NA for occurrence records (string)

Label: Sampling Method
Description: How the organism was observed or sampled: photo, d-frame net sediment sampling, Shocking or Seine (string)

Label: Site Key
Description: Key of the site: its latitude and longitude rounded to four decimals, joined by a vertical bar (string)

Label: State Abbreviation
Description: Two-letter postal abbreviation of the state (string)

Label: State FIPS
Description: Two-digit state FIPS code (string)

Label: State FIPS
Description: Two-digit state FIPS code (string)

Label: State Name
Description: Name of the state the county lies in (string)

Label: Synthetic Location
Description: Flag marking a link whose location is synthetic, as named by the source; only the value true occurs (boolean)

Label: Wikidata ID
Description: Wikidata QID of the species (e.g., Q613939); the text NA where none is recorded (string)

Label: Subject Of
Description: URL of the iNaturalist observation behind an older-layer OBSERVED_AT link, on its reified statement (IRI)

Label: Observed At
Description: Relates a wildlife species observation to the geographic location where it was observed. Part of the older KN-Wildlife layer (wildlife.proto-okn.net namespace), which is separate from the Observation model.

Label: Observed At
Description: Relates a wildlife species observation to the geographic location where it was observed. Part of the older KN-Wildlife layer (wildlife.proto-okn.net namespace), which is separate from the Observation model.

Label: Observed Times
Description: Number of times the species was observed at the location, on the reified OBSERVED_AT link (int)
